answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded collateral and correlated-equivocation accounting: if k identities coordinate conflicting votes, aggregate penalties grow as O(k^2), rather than merely linearly. Detection can also trigger asymmetric depreciation across linked escrows, compounding losses by an exponential multiplier, so adding aliases worsens the attacker’s total exposure. This raises costs over the protocol’s horizon; a garden of identities offers no shelter when shared control is exposed as hollow.
